outline.chapter_title: 1. Foundations: The Legacy and Limitations of LSTMs
outline.description: This chapter revisits the history of RNNs and LSTMs, explaining the core mechanisms that made them successful for decades. It critically analyzes the three fundamental limitations of the original LSTM architecture that hindered scaling to modern model sizes: the inability to revise storage decisions, limited scalar storage capacity, and sequential processing due to memory mixing.
subtopics: History of Recurrent Neural Networks and the Vanishing Gradient Problem
Core LSTM Mechanics: Constant Error Carousel, Gates, and Cell States
Limitation (i): Inability to Revise Storage Decisions (The Nearest Neighbor Search Problem)
Limitation (ii): Limited Storage Capacities (Scalar vs. Complex Memory)
The Rise of Transformers and State Space Models as responses to LSTM limits

outline.chapter_title: 2. Evolving the Architecture: Exponential Gating and Memory Mixing
outline.description: This chapter introduces the first major extension to the LSTM family: sLSTM. It details how replacing sigmoid gates with exponential gates enables dynamic revision of stored information via normalization. It also explores the concept of memory mixing through multiple heads and cells, establishing a new paradigm for state tracking.
subtopics: Exponential Gating: Replacing Sigmoids with Exp Activations
Stabilization Techniques: Normalizer States and Stabilizer States
The Mechanism of Revising Storage Decisions
Memory Mixing via Multiple Memory Cells and Heads
Verification: Output Equivalence despite Gate Modification

outline.chapter_title: 3. Expanding Capacity: The Matrix Memory mLSTM
outline.description: This chapter covers the second major extension, mLSTM. It explains how upgrading from scalar cell states to matrix memories allows for dense associative recall. The algorithm integrates bidirectional associative memory principles with covariance update rules to significantly increase information storage density while enabling full parallelization.
subtopics: From Scalars to Matrices: Conceptualizing Matrix Memory
Bidirectional Associative Memories (BAMs) in Modern Contexts
**The Covariance Update Rule**: Optimal Storage vs. Retrieval
**Key-Value Pairs**: Precise Representation in High Dimensions
**Query Mechanisms**: Retrieving Information via Dot Products

outline.chapter_title: **4.** System Design: xLSTM Blocks and Large-Scale Architectures
outline.description: **There is no chapter named "System Design"**. This chapter integrates sLSTM and mLSTM into practical deep learning architectures. It details how residual blocks are constructed differently for each variant (pre-up-projection vs. post-up-projection) based on their specific memory characteristics, leading to scalable xLSTM models.
